Let me work through this. The phase is "improvement". I must deliver a `design.decide_improvement` call. The accepted diagnosis: sampled settling failed (residual tip speed above speed limit), reach passed. Attribution statuses: settling_speed_limit_exceeded supported; update wall time insufficient_evidence; reduced effective horizon possible; cold-started plans possible; reach geometry failure ruled out; one-step projection model mismatch possible.

The grant: three variables — components/far/length_m [0.11,0.13], components/near/length_m [0.15,0.17], design/section_scale [0.95,1.05], plus design/material_scenario choice (baseline/compliant/stiff). Wait, editable scope lists parameters including design/material_scenario and design/section_scale. The instructions say "original three-variable geometry grant" — near length, far length, section scale. Material scenario is a semantic decision; the instruction says "Controller weights, materials, force limits and task changes are not authorized." So materials excluded. So the three variables: near length, far length, section_scale.

The previous report's recommendations both defer. The diagnosis says the supported cause is settling speed limit exceeded; the residual speed cause is not attributed. Should I adopt a geometry change? The instruction: "Do not force a geometry change to consume the allowance." The diagnosis has no geometry-linked cause — reach_geometry_failure is ruled out. The possible causes are horizon/warm-start/projection model, none of which are within the geometry grant. Increasing section scale / lengths would change stiffness and inertia, plausibly affecting settling speed, but there is no supporting evidence linking geometry to residual tip speed. So defer is the justified disposition — with empty changes.

Instructions: "adopt with an explicit justified delta, or defer/reject with empty changes." So defer with changes: {} (empty). Expected measurable effects stated separately for reach, sampled holding, and computation; uncertainty allowed.

Let me also consider: do I need any evidence reads? Evidence turn limit is 0, and I have the report content. Phase tools include evidence.read, but phase budget is model_calls 3, tool_calls 44. evidence_turn_limit: 0 means... "When the read allowance ends, deliver the current phase using its remaining advertised handoff tool." I think I should just deliver. Actually, I could do one evidence read, but the read allowance is 0, so no reads available. So deliver directly.

Now the call: design.decide_improvement with disposition "defer", rationale, expected_measurable_effect, and changes empty (omit or {}). Changes is not required.

Should I reference fact handles? "Select fact_handles for your own concise factual statements." The tool schema for design_decide_improvement is flat: disposition, rationale, expected_measurable_effect, changes. There's no fact_handle field in the schema. Hmm — the system says "Select fact_handles for your own concise factual statements" but the tool's parameters don't include a fact_handles field. additionalProperties false for the object, so I can't add a fact_handles key. Hmm... Actually "changes" has additionalProperties true. But that's for candidate builder paths. Better to not put fact handles in changes since changes must be empty on defer.

Hmm, but the instruction says select fact_handles. Maybe I can embed handles in rationale prose? The host expands exact internal references. I'll cite handles inline in rationale text. That seems safest — reference handles like f5a78f2ff99df etc. But those handles are from the fact catalog presented here. Let me embed a handful of relevant handles in the rationale.

Relevant handles: settling failure (fc5b0de5671bc sampled_settling_passed false), terminal_speed (f7f96eef8a315), speed limit (f6c63688b547f), reach passed (fa2df53ca3437), terminal error (f9b10abd95f4f), reach tolerance (fd0407340762b), late max error/speed (f5a78f2ff99df, f69887e2a8ae5), effective horizon facts (fd45cb2a843b4, f946ece9a31f4), horizon configured (f3abe564a036e), stopping counts (fdadd8fe6513d, f07ea946b5201), init/noninit (fed20e2cfb7d5, f03f310fff089), mean update (f12f519656d7c), control period (fdcd580c300c1), deadline misses (f4247d77f9243), limitations (f2d3a0144633d, fb00225d189d3), noninit (fbe0890f5519d).

Rationale: defer. Why: the accepted diagnosis's only supported cause is the sampled settling speed-limit exceedance; the candidate causes (reduced effective horizon, cold-started/truncated plans, one-step projection mismatch, wall-time deadline misses) are controller/timing/retention issues outside the three-variable geometry grant; reach failure was ruled out, so no geometry delta has evidence support. No counterfactual replay capability exists (capability gap), and the previous report deferred both recommendations. Forcing a geometry change would be unsupported.

Expected measurable effect: with no change adopted, expected effects are nil/unobservable; state separately: reach — no expected change (reach already passed with terminal error 0.00764 m below 0.01 m tolerance); sampled holding — no expected change, holding speed expected to remain far above 0.02 m/s limit; computation — no expected change in update wall time / effective horizon. Uncertainty allowed: any future geometry candidate's effect on settling speed is unquantified by available evidence.

Also should I note that defer leaves the execution allowance unused.

Now, "Use exactly one call, or up to three independent evidence reads." I'll make one call: design.decide_improvement.

Let me write the parameters.

disposition: "defer"
changes: {} — should I include? "defer/reject with empty changes." I'll pass changes: {} explicitly? The schema allows omitting; including empty object is fine and explicit. I'll include {}.

rationale: must be minLength 1. Include handles.

expected_measurable_effect: minLength 1, separate statements for reach, sampled holding, computation.

Let me draft.

rationale: "Accepted diagnosis records sampled_settling_passed false (fc5b0de5671bc) with terminal_speed_m_s 0.635 m/s (f7f96eef8a315) far above speed_limit_m_s 0.02 m/s (f6c63688b547f), while reach_passed true (fa2df53ca3437) with terminal_error_m 0.00764 m (f9b10abd95f4f) inside reach_tolerance_m 0.01 m (fd0407340762b); reach_geometry_failure is ruled out and no geometry-linked cause is supported. The possible contributors — reduced effective_horizon 1-7 below configured horizon 10 (fd45cb2a843b4, f3abe564a036e), 34 User_Requested_Stop vs 1 Solve_Succeeded (f07ea946b5201, fdadd8fe6513d) with initialization_selected 29 vs noninitialization_selected 6 (fed20e2cfb7d5, f03f310fff089), and the bounded-horizon projected one-step probe — are controller, timing and retention factors outside the near/far length and section_scale grant. No closed-loop counterfactual replay exists (capability gap) and full warm plans/iteration traces are not retained (f2d3a0144633d, full_snapshots_available f4e1e82ea1469), so any geometry delta would be an unsupported guess rather than a justified change; a geometry change is deliberately not forced to consume the execution allowance (fb00225d189d3)."

expected_measurable_effect: "Reach: no change expected — reach already passed (fa2df53ca3437) with terminal error 0.00764 m inside the 0.01 m tolerance (f9b10abd95f4f, fd0407340762b). Sampled holding: no change expected under this decision — recorded settle-window speeds (e.g. 1.4769184551353305 m/s and 0.6351726092425104 m/s, f69887e2a8ae5, f7f96eef8a315) are expected to stay far above the 0.02 m/s limit (f6c63688b547f) and sampled_settling_passed (fc5b0de5671bc) to remain false, since no parameter is changed. Computation: no change expected in mean_update_s 17.30 s (f12f519656d7c) or effective horizon, which are governed by controller/recipe settings outside this grant; any future candidate's effect is unquantified by current evidence."

That's good. Make one call.

Note: should I worry about "changes" requiring candidate builder paths? Empty is fine for defer.

Also I should not invent derived numerical facts — I'm reporting retrieved values, fine. "0.00764 m" is a rounded prose of retrieved value — allowed ("Rounded prose is allowed").

Make the call.
